categories.title: Power on and unlock
items: Turn the PC on from your phone with Wake-on-LAN.
Unlock the PC with your fingerprint or the phone's screen lock, even right after boot and before Avyn is open on the PC (optional).
Works with a PC that has no PIN, too.
Lock, sleep, restart and shut down the PC, with confirmation.

items: Stream one PC monitor to your phone over your local network, up to 720p at 30 fps.
Two-finger zoom and landscape full screen.
Draw arrows and ellipses or point with a highlighted pointer; they show up on the PC.
Switch monitors live. One phone at a time; Avyn tells you who is using it.

categories.title: TV and displays
items: Play on TV: send the video that is playing, or a file, to the TV.
Turn off the other displays while you watch.
Turn each monitor on or off, or all of them at once.
Samsung TV: power on and off over the network.
Move windows between monitors with a visual layout and previews.

categories.title: Media
items: Play, pause, next, previous, seek bar and 10-second jumps, with cover art and what is playing.
Auren: full screen, audio tracks and subtitles, and sync in 100 ms steps.

Edge and Chrome with the Avyn extension: full screen, speed, subtitles and audio (YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max, Apple TV and Prime Video) and the site's own buttons (skip intro, next episode, “Are you still watching?”).
Volume: level, steps and mute, reflecting changes made on the PC.

categories.title: Routines
items: Routines of up to 20 steps that run with one tap: open programs on the screen you choose, play on TV, volume, turn displays off, waits, and lock or sleep at the end.
Created and edited from the phone and shared across your phones.
If a step fails, it tells you which one and why.

categories.title: Touchpad and keyboard
items: Touchpad: move, click, double-click, right-click and two-finger scroll.
Adjustable pointer speed.
Remote keyboard with Unicode text, Enter, Backspace, Escape, Tab and arrows.
Shortcuts with Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Windows.

categories.title: Programs and windows
items: Open any Start menu program from your phone, with search and your recent ones on top.
List of open windows with search: focus, minimize, maximize, restore or close.
Icon, app and display for each window.

categories.title: Files
items: Browse the folders you share, with thumbnails, search (subfolders too) and sorting.
Download files or whole folders to the phone, with progress and free-space check.
Upload files to the PC, or share them from any Android app with the Share sheet.
Create folders and open files or folders on the PC.
You choose what is shared, with no executables or scripts.

categories.title: Karaoke with Kantaria
items: Library, queue, players, sessions and live scores from your phone.
History per session and per player.
Several phones at once, each seeing the others' changes.

categories.title: Several PCs and connection
items: Pair several PCs and switch between them; “Your PCs” lets you turn on, connect to or unlock each one.
Automatic reconnection when you return to the app or after a restart.
If it can't find the PC, connect by typing its IP.
Away from home, reconnect an already paired PC through its address inside a VPN (Tailscale or another).

categories.title: Security and privacy
items: Everything happens on your local network: no Avyn account and no cloud.
Each phone is approved on the PC with a verification code, and can be revoked at any time.
The phone only talks to your PC: it pins its certificate and accepts no other.
Secrets are stored encrypted (DPAPI on Windows, secure storage on Android).
Unlocking uses a separate service, a one-time challenge and five attempts per phone; your PIN never leaves without your fingerprint.
Programs, files, live screen and unlock can each be turned off from the PC.

categories.title: Convenience
items: The Agent lives in the Windows tray, starts with the system and updates itself without cutting a connection in use.
Spanish and English.
Extensions for Edge and Chrome.

security.title: Your PC. Your permission.
security.intro: Clear connections. Explicit choices. Security built around the devices you choose to use.

mechanisms.title: Pairing is explicit.
mechanisms.text: A phone must be paired with your PC before it can control it. You decide which devices belong: when pairing, the phone and the PC each show a verification code, and you approve only if they match.

mechanisms.title: Connections are encrypted.
mechanisms.text: Encryption protects communication between your paired phone and PC. It is one layer of protection, alongside device authorization.

mechanisms.title: Your PC recognizes your device.
mechanisms.text: Authorization is handled per device. Pairing does not mean opening control to everyone on your network.

mechanisms.title: The connection has an identity.
mechanisms.text: Certificate pinning ties the connection to the expected certificate, helping the phone recognize the Agent it paired with.

mechanisms.title: Access can be revoked.
mechanisms.text: Remove a device’s authorization when you no longer want it to control your PC.

mechanisms.title: Unlock is your choice.
mechanisms.text: Windows Unlock is opt-in. Enable it only if you want to use your phone for this action.

security.bandTitle: A shorter path between your devices.
security.bandText: Everyday control goes directly between your phone and PC on the local network. It does not require an Avyn account or an Avyn cloud service.
security.note: These mechanisms do not replace securing your phone, your PC and your network. Detailed protocol documentation and release-specific verification are still being prepared.

verify.intro: You should be able to understand how Avyn communicates. Here is the path to checking it for yourself.
verify.notice: This guide was verified on 22 October 2026 on Windows 11 with the direct download (Avyn Agent 0.1.0-alpha.42) and the Microsoft Store version (1.2.1.0), using an Android phone. Results may vary with your network, your Windows version and the Avyn version.

steps.title: Identify the Agent's connections.
steps.text: Avyn Agent runs as `Avyn.Agent.exe`. In the direct download it is in `%LocalAppData%\Avyn.Agent\current`; in the Microsoft Store version, inside `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps`. In PowerShell, `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess (Get-Process Avyn.Agent).Id` lists its TCP connections and `Get-NetUDPEndpoint -OwningProcess (Get-Process Avyn.Agent).Id` its UDP ports.

steps.title: Separate local traffic from external traffic.
steps.text: At rest, the Agent listens on TCP 47821 (connection with the phone) and UDP 47822 (discovery on your local network); the optional unlock service listens on TCP 47822. At startup, the Agent also probes TCP port 8002 on the addresses of your subnet (up to 254) to look for Samsung TVs, even if you have none paired: this is local traffic and does not leave your network. With a phone controlling the PC, we saw connections only from the phone's address (192.168.1.150 in the test) to port 47821.

steps.title: Understand the legitimate exceptions.
steps.text: In the direct download, the Agent checks for updates at startup and every 6 hours. In the test it contacted `api.github.com`, `github.com` and `release-assets.githubusercontent.com` on port 443; GitHub receives your PC's IP address, as any website does. The Microsoft Store version does not declare Internet access and, in 80 seconds of observation, opened no connections: the Store updates it. If a Samsung TV is present, the Agent talks to it inside your network. For now there is no setting to turn off the update check; if you do not want it to run, block the Agent's Internet access (next step).

steps.title: Restrict Internet with Windows Firewall.
steps.text: From an administrator PowerShell, this rule blocks the Agent's outbound connections to the Internet and keeps the local network: `New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Avyn Agent - sin Internet' -Direction Outbound -Program 'RUTA\Avyn.Agent.exe' -Action Block -RemoteAddress Internet`. Replace `RUTA` with the path of your installation. To undo it: `Remove-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Avyn Agent - sin Internet'`. In the test, with the rule in place, the Agent's connections to GitHub no longer left the PC; Windows still queried DNS for those names, because a system service makes those queries, not the Agent. Also, the first time the direct download runs, Windows shows a firewall prompt; until it is allowed, the phone cannot connect. With the rule in place the Agent cannot check for updates either: install new versions manually.

steps.title: Repeat everyday actions.
steps.text: With the Microsoft Store version, an already paired phone and the blocking rule in place, pointer control, volume and browsing the shared folders worked. Also try pairing, file transfers and unlocking with the rule in place, and record what works, what changes and which product version you used.

steps.title: Read the source code.
steps.text: Avyn's source code is still private. The public repository `github.com/pablopramparo/avyn-releases` only contains the installers and the update manifest. We will add a link to the code once it is public.

verify.bandText: This guide lists the tested versions, the conditions and the limitations. It does not claim that every feature works with all Internet traffic blocked: check the ones you use.
